concept.name: Stablecoin
concept.definition: A crypto-asset that aims to maintain a stable value relative to a specified asset — typically a fiat currency such as the U.S. dollar — or a pool or basket of assets, using a stabilization mechanism such as reserve backing. A 'global stablecoin' (GSC) is a stablecoin with potential reach and adoption across multiple jurisdictions.
concept.intuition: A stablecoin tries to be the steady dollar of the crypto world: a token engineered to be worth the same tomorrow as today, usually by backing each token with reserves.
concept.mechanics: Fiat-backed stablecoins hold reserve assets (cash, deposits, T-bills) and offer redemption at par; crypto-collateralized designs hold overcollateralized on-chain positions; algorithmic designs adjust supply incentives without full backing. The FSB's high-level recommendations call for a robust legal claim for users, timely redemption at par for single-fiat GSCs, an effective stabilization mechanism, and prudential requirements to mitigate run risk.
concept.failure_modes: Stablecoins can depeg and suffer runs when reserves are doubted or redemption is impaired — from the March 2023 USDC depeg during the banking stress to the total collapse of the uncollateralized TerraUSD in 2022. Reserve opacity, concentration in the banking system, and redemption gates are recurring vulnerabilities.
concept.misconceptions: That all stablecoins are equivalently stable — mechanisms range from fully reserved fiat-backed designs to purely algorithmic ones with no redemption claim, and only the mechanism and reserve quality underpin the peg. Also, 'stable value' is an objective, not a guarantee.
concept.example: A USD stablecoin issuer holds roughly $1 of Treasury bills and deposits for every token outstanding and honors same-day redemption at $1.00 per token.
